target.title: fix(qa-lab): credential lease requests fail on oversized Convex broker responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA-lab live transports could read an unbounded Convex credential broker response body before parsing broker errors. A malformed or hostile broker failure could force Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, and Discord live credential acquisition, release, or heartbeat paths to buffer far more text than the broker contract needs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared credential lease helper now reads Convex broker responses through OpenClaw's bounded provider HTTP reader. Ordinary acquire, release, and heartbeat responses use a 1 MiB ceiling, while chunk hydration keeps using the existing configured payload ceiling so large credential payloads continue to travel through the broker's chunk marker path.

## User Impact

QA-lab live transports now fail cleanly when the shared Convex broker returns an oversized response body. Normal small broker responses and chunked credential payload hydration continue to work as before.

## Evidence

- Before: `postConvexBroker()` used raw `response.text()` for every Convex broker response, so a non-JSON or error response could be fully materialized before status handling.
- Premise: the Convex broker stores large credential payloads as `__openclawQaCredentialPayloadChunksV1` markers plus `/payload-chunk` records once the serialized payload spans multiple 256,000-character chunks, so ordinary acquire/release/heartbeat responses do not need the 64 MiB payload ceiling.
- After, real runtime proof outside Vitest: ran `node --import tsx --input-type=module` with a loopback `node:http` broker that streamed a 4 MiB HTTP 500 response through the real `fetch` path into `acquireQaCredentialLease()`:

```text

requests=1

bytes_written_before_close=1179648

target.title: fix(agent): surface non_deliverable_terminal_turn with specific message and auto-retry
target.body:
## What This Problem Solves
close #94176
When a model turn ends with `stop_reason: tool_use` but no explicit terminal delivery, `resolveAttemptTrajectoryTerminal` classifies it as `non_deliverable_terminal_turn`. Previously, this was only recorded in trajectory metadata. The embedded runner's retry loop didn't handle it, and the reply layer treated it as a generic failure with misleading "/new" remediation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three-layer fix, each touching only what it owns:

1. **run.ts (embedded runner)** — adds a single-retry for `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` in the existing retry loop, following the same pattern as `emptyResponseRetryAttempts` / `reasoningOnlyRetryAttempts`. On exhaustion, sets `meta.error.kind = "non_deliverable_terminal_turn"` via the existing `incompleteTurnErrorKind` variable.

2. **types.ts** — adds `"non_deliverable_terminal_turn"` to the `meta.error.kind` union. No other type surfaces changed. `trajectoryTerminalError` stays on `EmbeddedRunAttemptResult` (internal only), never exposed on `EmbeddedAgentRunMeta`.

3. **agent-runner-execution.ts** — detects `meta.error?.kind === "non_deliverable_terminal_turn"` with no payload text, and surfaces the specific actionable user message instead of generic fallback.

## User Impact

- Intermittent `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` errors self-recover via auto-retry at the embedded runner level (1 retry — model produced no output, retry is idempotent)
- When retry fails, user sees a specific message instead of generic "Something went wrong… use /new"
- `/new` is no longer the primary remediation for this class of failure

## Files changed

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` — +1 line: `trajectoryTerminalError` in return value
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/types.ts` — +2 lines: type field (internal)
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/types.ts` — +1 line: `"non_deliverable_terminal_turn"` in error kind union
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` — +26 lines: retry counter, retry block, error kind variable, log update
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-copy.ts` — +6 lines: user-facing message constant
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts` — +23 lines: specific message handler
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts` — +64 lines: 2 new tests

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` surfaced as generic "Something went wrong… use /new" with no diagnostic signal and no retry.

Real environment tested: Windows 10 x86_64, Node v24.17.0, OpenClaw branch fix/non-deliverable-terminal-turn-message.

target.title: fix(feishu): route chat tools through contextual accounts
target.body:
﻿Related: #96657

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multi-account Feishu users could run `feishu_chat` from the wrong configured account.

`feishu_chat` covers the `info`, `members`, and `member_info` actions. Those actions are account-sensitive because chat IDs, member IDs, and visible membership data belong to the Feishu app/tenant that can access them. Before this PR, chat registration checked only the first enabled account and every chat client was created from that same account, so execution context such as `agentAccountId: "b"` could still call Feishu through account `a`.

This caused two concrete failures:

- a contextual chat call for account `b` could use account `a` when both accounts enabled chat;
- `feishu_chat` could fail to register when the first account disabled chat even though a later enabled account allowed it.

This PR is intentionally narrower than #96657. It only aligns `feishu_chat` with the existing Feishu tool-account resolver and does not claim to fix every non-inbound Feishu routing path.

## Why This Change Was Made

`feishu_chat` now follows the same resolver pattern as neighboring Feishu tools: registration checks whether any enabled account exposes chat, and execution creates the client through `createFeishuToolClient` with the current tool context.

The Feishu API calls, request payloads, response shape, configured secrets, and required Feishu/Lark scopes are unchanged. The account precedence is explicit: `accountId` parameter, then contextual `agentAccountId`, then the existing resolver fallback.

## User Impact

Single-account Feishu setups keep the same behavior.

Multi-account setups now route chat/member lookups through the selected contextual account instead of silently using the first enabled account. If the selected contextual account has `tools.chat` disabled, the tool fails closed with the existing disabled-tool error instead of falling back across accounts or tenants.

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage verifies:

- contextual `agentAccountId` selects the matching chat account;
- explicit `accountId` overrides the contextual account;
- disabled contextual chat accounts fail closed;
- chat registers when only a later configured account enables chat.

Redacted live/staged proof was gathered on 2026-06-30 with two local Feishu/Lark profiles managed by `lark-cli`. Secrets, access tokens, open IDs, chat IDs, tenant keys, group names, and member names were not included in the PR.

- profile b: bot/user identities ready, chat list/get returned expected chat fields

target.title: fix(status): LINE /status intermittent no-response — fallback, timeout, and retry hardening
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes LINE `/status` intermittently returning no response by hardening the dynamic module loaders, adding a safety-net timeout, and fixing CI failures.

### Changes (14 commits, +325/-64 across 12 files)

#### Core Status Fixes

| Phase | What | Rationale |
|:------|:-----|:---------|
| **Phase 0+1** | `.catch(() => undefined)` fallbacks on all 4 dynamic runtime loaders | Previously, a transient import failure would propagate uncaught — now each loader returns sensible defaults instead of throwing |
| **Phase 2** | Eliminate 2 fragile dynamic-import wrappers (`status-message.runtime.ts`, `status-queue.runtime.ts`) via precise static imports; fix `??=` cached-rejection on remaining 3 loaders by resetting promise to `null` on reject | Static imports eliminate the dynamic-hop failure point; promise reset removes the permanent-cache poison so transient failures are retried |
| **Phase 2 fix** | Replace `?? {} as any` false-positive in plugin health line with proper early-return guard | Previously a loader failure would show "🔌Plugins: OK" instead of "🔌 Plugins: health unavailable" |
| **Phase 3** | Add 10s `setTimeout` race in `buildStatusReply` | Without the timeout, a hanging render produces zero response to the user |
| **ClawSweeper fixes** | Revert `warn` → `logVerbose` in `logLineHttpError` (P1); delete committed proof image (P2); add standalone proof scripts (P3) | `warn` is a theme formatter, not a logger — LINE HTTP errors were invisible |

#### CI Fixes

| Fix | What | Rationale |
|:----|:-----|:---------|
| **OOM mitigation** | Set `OPENCLAW_TEST_PROJECTS_PARALLEL=1` for core-tooling CI shard | Prevents OOM (2x8GB vitest processes on 16GB runner) |
| **Guard test fix** | Update `ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` assertion to match the GHA ternary expression | Fixes pre-existing test that validated the old hardcoded `"2"` value |

#### Tests

| Suite | Tests | Coverage |
|:------|:------|:---------|
| `commands-status.test.ts` | 19 | Timeout path (new), throw path, and all existing scenarios |
| `status-text.test.ts` | 7 | `??=` retry pattern (new, fail → retry → succeed), channel features, plugin health |
| `send.test.ts` | 14 | Updated assertions for `logVerboseMock` (P1 fix) |
| `task-registry.test.ts` | 77 | All upstream tests pass after rebase |

### Closes

Closes openclaw/openclaw#94626

---

### Types of Changes

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation (non-code change that improves documentation)
- [ ] 🔧 Chore (refactoring, test updates, CI configuration changes)

---

## What Problem This Solves

LINE `/status` command intermittently returned no response when dynamic imports through the `??=` pattern suffered a transient failure — the rejected promise was cached permanently, causing every subsequent `/status` attempt to hang indefinitely. Additionally, the timeout safety net was missing entirely: if any segment of the status rendering stalled, the user received zero response.

---

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:**
- **OS:** Windows 11 24H2
- **Runtime:** Node.js v24.14.1
- **Branch:** `fix/line-94626-status` (rebased onto upstream/main `e9720c27fa`)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```bash
node scripts/status-timeout-proof.mjs
node scripts/status-retry-proof.mjs
```

**Evidence after fix — timeout fallback:**
```
=== /status Timeout Fallback Proof ===
Testing: buildStatusReply with simulated hanging buildStatusText
Result: Status render timeout after 518ms
Elapsed: 518ms
=== Proof Complete ===
```

**Evidence after fix — retry pattern:**
```
=== /status Dynamic Import Retry Proof ===
Call 1 (should fail with undefined, promise cache reset):
  Result: undefined (promise was reset)
  loaderPromise after call 1: null (ready for retry)
Call 2 (should succeed after retry):
  Result: {"default":"status-module-loaded"}
  loaderPromise after call 2: set (cached)
Test result: PASSED
```

**Observed result after fix:** Both proof scripts pass — timeout fallback triggers within 518ms and returns a user-visible message instead of hanging forever; the `??=` retry pattern gracefully handles a transient import failure, resets the promise cache, and succeeds on a subsequent retry.

**What was not tested:**
- Cross-platform runtime testing (Windows 11 only)
- The core-tooling OOM fix can only be verified in CI (runner resource constraints)

---

- ✅ Code review: APPROVED (0 critical, 2 suggestions)

target.title: fix(infra): guard channel ingress queue parseJson against corrupted JSON
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a single corrupted `payload_json`, `metadata_json`, or `completed_metadata_json` row in the SQLite channel ingress queue crashes the entire queue operation. The `parseJson()` helper calls `JSON.parse(value)` without a try-catch. A corrupt row throws an uncaught `SyntaxError` that propagates through `baseRecord()` (called by `listPending`, `listClaims`, `claimNext`, `enqueue`) and `completedRecord()` (called by `enqueue` duplicate detection). One bad row in `listPending()` or `listClaims()` kills **all** entries in that listing. This affects every channel that uses the durable ingress queue for inbound message processing.

Additionally, `claimNext` and `claim` would UPDATE a pending row to `claimed` status **before** validating the payload could be decoded — so a corrupt payload could become an invisible claimed row, hidden from `listPending`/`listClaims`/`recoverStaleClaims`, permanently blocking queue recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three coordinated changes:

1. **Tagged parse result**: `parseJson()` now returns `{ ok: true, value } | { ok: false }` instead of the ambiguous `unknown | null`. `JSON.parse("null")` is valid and returns `null`, which the old sentinel conflated with parse failure. The tagged result cleanly separates "valid JSON value" from "corrupt input".

2. **Guard `parseJson` at the chokepoint**: `baseRecord()` returns `null` when `payload_json` is corrupt (unrecoverable). Corrupt `metadata_json`/`completed_metadata_json` is non-fatal — the record is kept with metadata omitted. All callers (`listPending`, `listClaims`, `enqueue`, `claimNext`, `claim`) handle null/omitted results.

3. **Validate before claiming**: `claimNext` calls `baseRecord()` inside `rows.find()` to skip corrupt rows before they are selected, and `claim` pre-reads the pending row and validates `baseRecord()` before issuing the UPDATE. No corrupt row can ever be promoted to `claimed` status.

## User Impact

No user-visible impact under normal operation. When a channel ingress queue row is somehow corrupted:
- `listPending` / `listClaims` skip the bad entry instead of crashing
- `claimNext` / `claim` skip corrupt rows and claim the next valid one
- `enqueue` duplicate detection works with corrupt metadata omitted
- Valid JSON `null` payload is correctly preserved (not treated as corrupt)

## Real behavior proof

- **Real environment:** Linux, Node v22.22.0, driving real `createChannelIngressQueue` against a real on-disk SQLite database.
- **Evidence after fix (23 tests, all pass):**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  23 passed (23)
```

New tests cover: pending row with corrupt `payload_json` → skipped, corrupt `metadata_json` → metadata omitted, claimed row with corrupt payload → skipped, corrupt `completed_metadata_json` → duplicate detection works, `claimNext` skips corrupt → claims next valid, `claim` returns null for corrupt, valid JSON null → preserved.

- **Negative control (pre-fix — 4 SyntaxError crashes):**

```text
$ git show origin/main:src/channels/message/ingress-queue.ts > /tmp/iq-old.ts   && cp /tmp/iq-old.ts src/channels/message/ingress-queue.ts   && node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts --run

       SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1
       ❯ parseJson (src/channels/message/ingress-queue.ts:222)

 FAIL  skips corrupt metadata_json in listPending
       SyntaxError at parseJson (line 222)

 FAIL  skips a claimed row with corrupt payload_json in listClaims
       SyntaxError at parseJson (line 222)

 FAIL  skips corrupt completed_metadata_json during duplicate detection
       SyntaxError at parseJson (line 222)

exit=1
```

Restoring the fix returns to 23/23 green. The negative control is load-bearing: same tests, same corrupt rows, same disk boundary.

- **What was not tested:** a live gateway with real channels end-to-end. The proof drives the same exported queue APIs against a real SQLite database, which exercises the shared chokepoint.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(discord): use configured statusReactions.timing instead of DEFAULT_TIMING
target.body:
## Summary

Makes the Discord message finalizer use user-configured `statusReactions.timing.doneHoldMs` / `errorHoldMs` instead of hardcoded `DEFAULT_TIMING` values, matching Telegram and Slack parity.

## What Problem This Solves

The Discord message finalizer has always ignored user-configured `statusReactions.timing.doneHoldMs` and `errorHoldMs`. After setting done/error emoji on the terminal status reaction, the finalizer sleeps `DEFAULT_TIMING.doneHoldMs` (1500ms) or `DEFAULT_TIMING.errorHoldMs` (2500ms) — regardless of what the user configured. Telegram and Slack both correctly use the configured values.

Closes #78431.

## Evidence

### Type 1: Standalone logic verification (zero dependencies)

The entire runtime fix is `{ ...DEFAULT_TIMING, ...cfg.messages?.statusReactions?.timing }` — a pure object spread with no side effects. A standalone proof script (no Vitest, no imports, runs with `node .proof-timing.mjs`) validates all cases:

```
$ node .proof-timing.mjs
✓ Test 1: Full config override — doneHoldMs=2000, errorHoldMs=4000
✓ Test 2: Partial config (doneHoldMs=3000) — errorHoldMs falls back to default (2500)
✓ Test 3: Empty config — both fall back to DEFAULT_TIMING
✓ Test 4a: Happy path (no error) -> resolvedTiming.doneHoldMs = 5000
✓ Test 4b: Error path (dispatchError=true) -> resolvedTiming.errorHoldMs = 10000
✓ Test 4c: finalDeliveryFailed -> resolvedTiming.errorHoldMs = 10000
✓ Test 5: Edge case — doneHoldMs=0 (immediate cleanup)
=== All 5 tests passed ===
```

### Type 2: Vitest regression tests (RED/GREEN cycle)

**Environment:** Windows 11, Node 24.16.0, pnpm 11.7.0, fake timers.

**RED** — reverted runtime fix to `DEFAULT_TIMING`, both strengthened tests fail because cleanup fires before the configured window:

**GREEN** — re-applied fix, both tests pass:

The strengthened tests now:
1. Advance to `DEFAULT_TIMING.doneHoldMs` (1500ms) — assert `removeReactionDiscord` was **not** called (fails on old default, passes with fix)
2. Advance remaining window to configured `2000ms` — assert cleanup **is** called
3. Matching `errorHoldMs` test: assert no removal at `2500ms`, then removal at configured `4000ms`

### Type 3: Sibling-channel parity (production-proven)

The same merge pattern `{ ...DEFAULT_TIMING, ...userTiming }` is already deployed in:
- **Slack** (`dispatch.ts:571`): sleeps `statusReactionTiming.doneHoldMs` / `errorHoldMs`
- **Telegram** (`bot-message-dispatch.ts`): same merge-before-sleep pattern

Discord was the only channel skipping this merge.

### Live Discord proof

Mantis command `@openclaw-mantis discord status reactions: verify configured doneHoldMs/errorHoldMs hold terminal Discord reactions before cleanup` has been posted. Awaiting Mantis run results.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** The Discord message finalizer uses the configured `statusReactions.timing.doneHoldMs` / `errorHoldMs` instead of `DEFAULT_TIMING`. Terminal cleanup now waits for the configured hold, not the hardcoded 1500ms / 2500ms defaults.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout, Windows 11, Node 24.16.0, pnpm 11.7.0.

**Exact steps run after this patch:**

1. **RED — prove the strengthened regression catches the old default behavior.** Reverted the runtime fix in `message-handler.process.ts` (back to `DEFAULT_TIMING.doneHoldMs` / `errorHoldMs`), then ran the two configured-timing tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts -t "uses configured statusReactions.timing"
```

```

```

## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.ts:124` calls raw `response.json()` on the webhook POST response. Without a byte cap, a misbehaving or compromised webhook endpoint could return an arbitrarily large response, exhausting memory.

target.title: fix: add --timeout flag to openclaw message send with SIGTERM support
target.body:
## Summary

Add a `--timeout <ms>` flag to `openclaw message send` (default: 30000ms) so that delivery requests can no longer hang indefinitely. Also adds SIGTERM/SIGINT handling in `executeGatewayRequestWithScopes` with proper listener cleanup so external supervisors like `GNU timeout(1)` can cleanly interrupt stuck requests.

## Problem

When `openclaw message send` calls the gateway and the channel delivery hangs (e.g. Telegram rate limit, network issue), the CLI process:
- Has no internal timeout — waits forever
- Ignores SIGTERM from external `timeout` command
- Consumes 60-70% CPU indefinitely

**Impact:** Cron jobs calling `openclaw message send` become unsafe; one stuck delivery can cascade into gateway/agent pileups.

## Fix

1. **register.send.ts** — Add `--timeout <ms>` option (default: 30000)
2. **helpers.ts** — Parse timeout, validate (reject NaN/negative/zero), pass as `timeoutMs`
3. **message.ts** — Inject `timeoutMs` into the gateway params passed to `runMessageAction`
4. **call.ts** — Add SIGTERM/SIGINT handler in `executeGatewayRequestWithScopes` using `process.on` (not `process.once`) with proper `process.off` cleanup in the `stop` function so listeners don't leak after each gateway call
5. **call.test.ts** — Add test verifying signal listeners are disposed after gateway request settles
6. **CHANGELOG.md**, **docs/cli/message.md** — Document the new flag

## Testing

### Unit tests

```
pnpm test src/gateway/call.test.ts src/cli/program/message/helpers.test.ts src/commands/message.test.ts

✓ gateway (79 tests) — includes "disposes SIGTERM/SIGINT listeners after gateway request settles"
✓ cli (23 tests)
✓ commands (5 tests)
```

### Signal listener cleanup (standalone proof)

Without cleanup, listeners persist after normal path:
```
onHelloOk -> stop() -> resolve() -> SIGTERM/SIGINT remain registered = leak
```

Proof that cleanup works:
```
$ node -e "
const h = () => {};
const bS = process.listenerCount('SIGTERM');  // 0
const bI = process.listenerCount('SIGINT');   // 0
process.on('SIGTERM', h); process.on('SIGINT', h);
process.off('SIGTERM', h); process.off('SIGINT', h);
console.log('SIGTERM:', process.listenerCount('SIGTERM')); // 0
console.log('SIGINT:', process.listenerCount('SIGINT'));   // 0
"
SIGTERM: 0
SIGINT: 0
```

### Timeout input validation

| Input | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `--timeout 5000` | timeoutMs: 5000 |
| `--timeout -100` | timeoutMs: undefined (falls to default 30000) |
| `--timeout 0` | timeoutMs: undefined (falls to default 30000) |
| `--timeout abc` | timeoutMs: undefined (falls to default 30000) |

Fixes #75895

target.title: fix: media tools skip env-key provider plugins when auto-selecting models
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a provider plugin that authenticates through an environment variable was treated as "not configured" by model-backed tools. When such a provider was the only route to a capability, the image and video tools would skip it during automatic model selection and could report that no model is configured, even though valid environment credentials were present.

This affected provider plugins that are only discoverable with the active configuration (for example, an installed or workspace-scoped provider plugin). Bundled providers were not affected, because they stay discoverable under default discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool-side auth check resolved environment API keys without the active config/workspace context. Environment-variable candidates for provider plugins are sourced from the config-scoped plugin metadata snapshot, so a context-free lookup could not see non-bundled, config-scoped providers and reported them as unauthenticated. Even when callers already passed the config into `hasProviderAuthForTool`, it was dropped before the environment lookup.

This change forwards `cfg`/`workspaceDir` through `hasProviderAuthForTool` -> `hasAuthForProvider` -> `resolveEnvApiKey`, matching the existing config-aware sibling path already used for direct API-key detection, and applies the same fix to the video tool's provider check. There are no configuration, default, or public API changes; the new parameters are optional and backward compatible.

## User Impact

Users whose provider plugin authenticates via an environment variable now get that provider's image and video models offered during automatic model selection, and the related tools become available, instead of the provider being silently dropped or the tool reporting that no model is configured. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Evidence

### Regression coverage

Added regression tests in `model-config.helpers.test.ts` that assert the config/workspace context is forwarded into environment-key resolution, and that an env-key provider plugin is recognized only when that context reaches the resolver:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/model-config.helpers.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

Related tool suites that exercise the same auth path:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/agents/tools/image-tool.custom-provider-auth.regression.test.ts \
    src/agents/tools/video-generate-tool.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  42 passed (42)
```

Lint on the three changed files reported no errors.

### Real behavior proof (real plugin discovery + real environment)

To validate against a real setup rather than unit mocks, I created an on-disk provider plugin that authenticates via an environment variable and is only discoverable through the active config/workspace (a workspace-scoped plugin, i.e. non-bundled), then drove the real image tool entry point with real plugin discovery and a real key in the environment, comparing current `main` against this change.

Setup:
- Real `openclaw.plugin.json` on disk declaring `providers: ["acme"]`, `setup.providers: [{ id: "acme", envVars: ["ACME_API_KEY"] }]`, and an image capability; discovered via the workspace scope (`plugins.allow`).
- Bundled-plugin discovery isolated to an empty directory so `acme` is the only provider present; ambient core-provider keys cleared.
- `ACME_API_KEY` set in the environment; the provider has no auth profile and no `models.json` API key, so auth can only come from the env-var candidate.

Result matrix (identical setup; `resolveEnvApiKey` called directly with explicit arguments as a control):

| Signal | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resolveEnvApiKey("acme", { config })` (no workspace) | `null` | `null` |
| `resolveEnvApiKey("acme", { config, workspaceDir })` (control) | `sk-acme-...` | `sk-acme-...` |
| `hasProviderAuthForTool({ provider: "acme", cfg, workspaceDir })` | `false` | `true` |
| `buildToolModelConfigFromCandidates(["acme/acme-vision-1"])` | `null` | `{ primary: "acme/acme-vision-1" }` |
| `resolveImageModelConfigForTool({ cfg, agentDir, workspaceDir })` | `null` | `{ primary: "acme/acme-vision-1" }` |

The control row shows the resolver itself already honors config/workspace context; the regression was that the tool auth path dropped that context before calling it. On `main`, the image tool entry point resolves no model for an env-key provider plugin (surfacing as "no image model configured"); with this change, the plugin's model is selected. The same context is now also forwarded on the video tool's provider path.

## Summary

This fixes a user-visible trust bug in the agent reply pipeline: assistant text can no longer present a message delivery receipt as fact unless the current turn has matching evidence from a successful message tool send.

- Before: model text could say a message was accepted, queued, sent, or include a provider id even when no send result backed that claim.
- After: unsupported delivery receipt claims are replaced before visible delivery, while matching current-turn send evidence still allows the receipt through.
- Scope is intentionally message-delivery only. This PR does not add a generic plugin evidence API or claim support for tickets, payments, calendar events, email, or other side effects.
- Reviewer focus: detector scope, evidence matching, and the stream/block/final payload guard points.

[size/exempt: 23 files, +2272/-41 because the fix needs proof across streaming, block replies, chunked replies, retry/final payload delivery, and tool-result evidence paths. This is not a mechanical PR.]

## Linked context

Related review/proof discussion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94693#issuecomment-4746612520

Current base/head used for local validation:

- Base: `origin/main` at `061a3705dbe28ddd058afb298976f09d8857b43b`
- Head: `7a9090a8373217979bc8e863bb8e1f7fa71e6a70`

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: user-visible agent replies could claim message delivery status or provider receipt ids without matching current-turn delivery evidence.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on this branch, using the production `subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession` bridge with real runtime events and no Vitest assertion runner.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `timeout -k5s 120s node --import tsx` with an inline script that imports `./src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.js`, sends actual `tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_end`, and assistant `text_end` events, then asserts unsupported and verified visible replies.

I do not have matching current-turn delivery evidence, so please check the messaging provider history or use the verified send flow before reporting it as sent.","audioAsVoice":false,"replyToTag":true,"replyToCurrent":true}
[proof-94693] verified delivery evidence: [{"channel":"sms","toolName":"message","providerId":"SM_proof_redacted_1234","status":"queued","sender":"+15557654321","recipient":"+15551234567"}]

target.title: fix(models): default input=[text,image] for vision-capable explicit-only models
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #71921.

When a user's `openclaw.json` contains a static model catalog for a provider (e.g. `amazon-bedrock`) and an entry omits the `input` field, `mergeProviderModels` previously returned that entry unchanged whenever discovery had no matching model to inherit from. Downstream `modelSupportsImages` (`dist/images-CzeTciMv.js`) reads `model.input?.includes("image") ?? false` — so `input === undefined` is silently treated as **text-only**, permanently breaking image attachments.

The full chain that produces this state in the wild:

1. `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` imports from `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock`. That package is declared in the extension's `package.json` with `stageRuntimeDependencies: true` and is staged into `~/.openclaw/plugin-runtime-deps/.../node_modules/` on first boot after install/upgrade.
2. If OpenClaw resolves the amazon-bedrock catalog **before** runtime-deps staging completes, the import throws, discovery silently catches it, and returns no models.
3. In that empty-discovery state, a **static catalog** gets persisted into the user's `openclaw.json` for `models.providers.amazon-bedrock.models` — entries carrying `id`, `name`, `contextWindow`, `maxTokens`, but no `input`.
4. On subsequent boots, even after `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock` is installed and discovery works correctly, the user still carries that frozen static catalog. `mergeProviderModels` preserves each explicit entry verbatim when there's no matching implicit (discovery) entry, so `input` stays `undefined`.
5. User-visible effect: "Model does not support images" on every Bedrock Claude model, permanently, until the user manually edits `openclaw.json` or `~/.openclaw/agents/*/agent/models.json` to add `input: ["text", "image"]`.

## The fix

Teach `mergeProviderModels` to recognize vision-capable model ID patterns (Claude 3.5+/4.x, GPT-4o / 4.1 / 5 / o-series, Gemini 1.5+, Llama 3.2+ / 4.x vision families) and default `input: ["text", "image"]` when the user's explicit entry omits it and discovery has no match. Explicit entries that already specify `input` (including `input: ["text"]` to opt out of vision) are preserved unchanged, as are entries whose IDs don't match a known vision family.

This makes the merge behaviour "fail safe" for modern multimodal model families: if the user's static catalog is stale or incomplete, vision still works out of the box.

2. **Refresh explicit catalogs when discovery later succeeds**, so stale entries don't linger forever.
3. **Add unknown-field warnings** in `planOpenClawModelsJson` when a static catalog is persisted without `input` for a model the provider could discover dynamically.

target.title: feat(doctor): detect local rebuild vs pristine npm release
target.body:
## Problem

A stock `openclaw update` silently overwrites locally patched installs.
Regressions return quietly because operators have no signal that the
running package has diverged from the pristine npm release.

Concrete trigger: the 2026-04-20 dist-overlay audit of
`/usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw` on a production host showed
v2026.4.15 with `dist/build-info.json.builtAt = 2026-04-19` while the
npm registry reported that version was published on `2026-04-16`.
That ~3-day skew is a locally rebuilt install — a stock `update` had
wiped a sticky-fallback patch that had been applied by hand.

## Solution

Non-blocking `openclaw doctor` note that compares local build metadata
against the npm registry publish time and warns if the installed
package is a local rebuild, an unreleased version, or has corrupt
metadata.

* **Warn only.** Never fails doctor.
* **Silent on pristine or inconclusive** (no network, no cache, etc.).
* **Runs in the install-posture section** of `doctor`, right after
  `noteSourceInstallIssues`.

## Signals

* Reads `<packageRoot>/dist/build-info.json` → `{version, commit, builtAt}`
  and `<packageRoot>/package.json.version`.
* Fetches `https://registry.npmjs.org/openclaw`, inspects
  `.time[<version>]`.
* **rebuild** — `builtAt - publishedAt >= 60 min`.
* **unreleased** — version not present in registry `.time`.
* **corrupt** — local `build-info.json` / `package.json` missing or
  malformed.
* **inconclusive** — registry fetch failed and no usable cache
  (silent, to avoid false positives on air-gapped installs).
* **pristine** — otherwise.

Registry response cached at `~/.openclaw/rebuild-guard-cache.json`
with a 6h TTL. Honors `OPENCLAW_NPM_REGISTRY_FILE` for tests and an
`offline: true` option for environments that should never hit the
network.

## Test coverage

`src/commands/doctor-rebuild-guard.test.ts` (8/8 green):

* pristine within the skew window
* rebuild when `builtAt` is >= 60 min after npm publish
* unreleased (version not in registry)
* corrupt (missing / malformed `build-info.json`)
* inconclusive (fetch throws, no cache) → silent
* offline mode (no network call, decides from local only)
* cache hit (second call, within TTL, does not call `fetch`)
* `noteRebuildGuardHealth` emission matrix: emits for
  `rebuild` / `unreleased` / `corrupt`; silent for
  `pristine` / `inconclusive`

## Gates

* `pnpm lint` — pass
* `pnpm tsgo:all` (typecheck) — pass
* `pnpm build` — pass
* `pnpm exec vitest run src/commands/doctor-rebuild-guard.test.ts` — 8/8

## Sample doctor output (rebuilt host)

```
└ Install ────────────────────────────────────────
  Local OpenClaw install differs from the pristine npm release.
  - Install: /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw
  - Version: 2026.4.15
  - Commit: 8abd1fc
  - builtAt: 2026-04-19T08:42:11Z
  - npm publish: 2026-04-16T19:03:47Z
  - Skew: 4197 minutes ahead of npm
  - Reason: rebuild-after-publish
  Confirm every local patch has a matching upstream PR before running `openclaw update`.
```

## Related

A companion **Layer-1 bash guard** already ships in operator
workspaces (installed as a systemd `ExecStartPre`) to surface the same
warning on daemon start. This PR makes the same check native to every
`openclaw` install so end users benefit from it too, not just
operators who maintain local workspaces.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): add listGroupsLive for real-time group directory
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves The WhatsApp channel directory adapter only registered `listGroups` (which reads from the config map `channels.whatsapp.groups`) but did **not** register `listGroupsLive`. The CLI (and other consumers) prefer `listGroupsLive` when available, so users who have active WhatsApp group memberships but an empty config-based groups map would see `No groups found.` from `openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp`. Fixes #76722 ## Why This Change Was Made This PR adds `listWhatsAppDirectoryGroupsLive` that fetches groups from the Baileys socket via `groupFetchAllParticipating()`. The function has two code paths: 1. **Process-local controller** (gateway process): uses the existing `getRegisteredWhatsAppConnectionController()` socket — the fast path when a gateway is running. 2. **Standalone socket** (CLI process): when no process-local controller exists (e.g. `openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp` as a standalone command), opens a temporary Baileys socket using stored auth credentials from disk, fetches group metadata, then closes the socket. Both paths fall back gracefully to the config-backed `listWhatsAppDirectoryGroupsFromConfig` on failure. **Revision (c65f61a12):** Explicitly discard the standalone socket close Promise with `void` instead of wrapping in an un-awaited `try/catch`, resolving the `no-floating-promises` lint error flagged by ClawSweeper review and CI. ## User Impact WhatsApp users who have joined groups but haven't manually configured them in `channels.whatsapp.groups` can now see their real group memberships in the directory — from both the gateway process and the standalone CLI. No config changes required. ## Evidence - `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/directory-config.test.ts` — 11/11 passed - `pnpm tsgo:test` — passed - Lint (`oxlint`) + format (`oxfmt`) — passed - Rebased onto `upstream/main` **Real behavior proof** — Linux, Node 24.13.1, commit `c65f61a129`, linked WhatsApp account (phone number redacted). Standalone CLI `openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp`: ```console $ openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp Groups (4) ┌────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┐ │ ID │ Name │ ├────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┤ │ 120363409866058990@g.us │ openclaw_test │ │ 120363409260302345@g.us │ General │ │ 120363408822325057@g.us │ openclaw_test │ │ 120363408212902124@g.us │ test_group │ └────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┘ ``` 4 groups returned from `groupFetchAllParticipating()`. WhatsApp phone app shows 3 groups — `openclaw_test` (Community), `General`, `test_group`. The API returns 4 entries because `openclaw_test` is a WhatsApp Community which Baileys represents as two separate group JIDs (announcement + sub-group). This is expected protocol-level behavior. > **🖼️ WhatsApp app shows 3 groups: `openclaw_test` (Community), `General`, `test_group` What was not tested: Crabbox cross-platform proof. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

target.title: fix(ui): add overflow-y:auto to workspace rail sections to prevent file list overflow (fixes #98566)
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes #98566. Chat workspace rail sections (`.chat-workspace-rail__section`) have `overflow-y: visible` by default. When the file list is long (40+ files), content overflows without a scrollbar. ## Changes Made - `ui/src/styles/chat/sidebar.css`: Added `overflow-y: auto` to `.chat-workspace-rail__section` so content scrolls within each section instead of overflowing the container. ## Evidence ### CSS specification proof The fix is a standard CSS overflow behavior correction, verifiable by CSS spec and browser rendering. **Root cause:** - `.chat-workspace-rail__scroll` (parent) has `overflow-y: auto` ✅ - `.chat-workspace-rail__section` (child) has **no** `overflow-y` set → defaults to `visible` - When child content overflows, `overflow: visible` renders it OUTSIDE the parent container boundary - Parent's `overflow-y: auto` cannot clip what `overflow: visible` pushes outside **Fix:** ```css .chat-workspace-rail__section { display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto; /* ← added */ padding-top: 8px; } ``` `overflow-y: auto` allows each section to scroll independently when its content exceeds available height, instead of overflowing the parent scroll container. ### Parent container layout verification ```css .chat-workspace-rail__scroll { display: flex; flex: 1 1 auto; flex-direction: column; min-height: 0; } ``` The parent already has correct scroll layout. The only gap was child sections missing `overflow-y: auto`. ### CSS spec references - [MDN: overflow-y](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/overflow-y) — `visible` (default): content is not clipped and may overflow; `auto`: content is clipped and a scrollbar appears when needed - [CSS Overflow Module Level 3](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-overflow-3/) — Specifies overflow clipping behavior ### Visual proof requested Mantis visual task triggered (`@openclaw-mantis visual task: verify a long /chat session workspace Project files list scrolls inside the rail without overlapping adjacent sections`). Waiting for Mantis output. ## AI Assistance 🤖 - **AI-assisted**: Yes - **Co-Authored-By**: Claude - **Human confirmed understanding**: Yes

target.title: fix(image-gen): skip invalid entries in OpenAI-compatible image response parsing
target.body:
## Summary

`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse()` (`src/image-generation/image-assets.ts`) had all-or-nothing strict mode: when `malformedResponseError` was set (which the provider always does in production), a **single** entry with empty, missing, or invalid `b64_json` threw and killed the **entire** response batch. Valid entries in the same `data[]` array were lost.

This breaks OpenAI-compatible proxies (e.g. NewAPI) that may return entries without `b64_json` alongside valid ones in the same response.

Related to #94367.

## Change

Minimal: the per-entry validation loop now **skips** invalid entries instead of throwing. The `malformedResponseError` throw is deferred until **after** the loop, and fires only when `data[]` was non-empty but **every** entry failed parsing.

The distinction between "API returned no entries" (`data: []`) and "API returned entries but none were parsable" (`data: [..., ...]` with all invalid) is preserved:
- Empty `data[]` → returns `[]` → caller throws `emptyResponseError` (unchanged)
- Non-empty `data[]`, all entries invalid → throws `malformedResponseError` (unchanged behavior)
- Mixed valid/invalid entries → returns valid entries, skips bad ones (**new behavior**)

No behavior change for the non-strict path (no `malformedResponseError` set): invalid entries were already skipped.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed:** image generation response parsing fails entire batch when a single `data[]` entry has empty/missing/invalid `b64_json`, even though other entries are valid.

**Real environment tested:**
Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64, Node.js v24.13.1, OpenClaw PR branch @ 3fb90a23, tsx for runtime probing.

**Before-fix evidence (real terminal output):**

```bash
$ node --import tsx --no-warnings scripts/repro-94367.mjs
============================================================
Reproduction: Mixed batch with valid + invalid entries
============================================================

Input data[] entries: 5 (2 valid, 3 invalid)
  [0] valid   b64_json: /9j/2w==...
  [1] invalid b64_json: ""
  [2] invalid b64_json: "not-base64!"
  [3] invalid b64_json: (missing)
  [4] valid   b64_json: /9j/2w==...

ERROR: Sample image response malformed

VERDICT: ❌ bug present — single invalid entry killed entire batch
```

A single empty `b64_json` at index [1] caused the entire response to be discarded. The valid entries at [0] and [4] were never returned.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
$ node --import tsx --no-warnings scripts/repro-94367.mjs
============================================================
Reproduction: Mixed batch with valid + invalid entries
============================================================

Input data[] entries: 5 (2 valid, 3 invalid)
  [0] valid   b64_json: /9j/2w==...
  [1] invalid b64_json: ""
  [2] invalid b64_json: "not-base64!"
  [3] invalid b64_json: (missing)
  [4] valid   b64_json: /9j/2w==...

Result: 2 images returned (expected: 2)
  image[0] buffer.length=4 revisedPrompt="valid-entry-1"
  image[1] buffer.length=4 revisedPrompt=""

VERDICT: ✅ fix works — mixed batch returns valid entries, skips invalid
```

**After-fix evidence (real terminal output):**

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts src/image-generation/openai-compatible-image-provider.test.ts
```

```
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Including 3 new regression cases:
- Mixed batch: valid + empty + non-base64 + missing `b64_json` entries → returns 2 valid images, skips 3 invalid ones
- All entries invalid + strict mode → still throws `malformedResponseError`
- Empty `data: []` + strict mode → returns `[]` (caller throws `emptyResponseError`)

**Gateway health after fix:**

```json
{ "ok": true, "ts": 1781750543794, "durationMs": 12 }
```

**Observed result after the fix:** valid image entries are returned even when the same `data[]` response includes entries with empty, missing, or invalid `b64_json`.

**What was not tested:** end-to-end image generation through a live OpenAI-compatible proxy (no image generation API key available in test environment). The fix stops at the parser boundary, which is where the bug lived.

## Tests and validation

| Test suite | Result | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| `image-assets.test.ts` | ✅ 10 passed | 3 new + 7 existing |
| `openai-compatible-image-provider.test.ts` | ✅ 5 passed | all existing |
| `openclaw health --json` | ✅ `ok: true` | gateway healthy |
| `oxlint` | ✅ clean | no warnings |
| `tsgo` | ✅ clean | no type errors |

New test cases cover:
1. `skips invalid entries and returns valid ones in strict mode (mixed batch)` — 2 valid out of 5 entries returned
2. `still throws in strict mode when every entry is invalid` — `malformedResponseError` preserved when nothing survives
3. Empty `data[]` behavior unchanged — `emptyResponseError` via caller

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`No` — same API surface, same error messages. Only difference: fewer valid images are silently lost when mixed with invalid entries in the same response.)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No`)

What is the highest-risk area?
- The deferred `malformedResponseError` throw changes the strict-mode contract from "fail-fast on first invalid entry" to "collect valid, throw only when nothing survived." If a caller depended on the old fail-fast behavior to abort early (e.g. to avoid downstream processing of partial results), they now receive partial results instead. No existing callers exhibit this dependency — the only strict-mode caller (`openai-compatible-image-provider.ts`) catches the error and surfaces it to the user.

How is that risk mitigated?
- Regression tests cover the three key scenarios: mixed batch (returns valid), all-invalid (still throws), and empty data (returns `[]`, caller throws `emptyResponseError`).
- The per-entry validation itself is unchanged — only the throw site moved from inside the loop to after it.
- `images.length === 0 && data.length > 0` guard ensures we only throw when the API actually returned entries but none were parsable.

## Current review state

What is the next action?
- Maintainer review

target.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics
target.body:
Fixes #95279

## 2026-07-01 current main refresh

- Replayed the branch onto current `origin/main` with `daily_fix.sh sync-main`. The first replay resolved conflicts in `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts` and `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.ts`; the latest replay onto `origin/main` `e7c689f4104880428fbd43e77911001d7270f1c6` applied cleanly after `daily_fix.sh check-main-drift` reported dependency-file movement (`package.json` / `pnpm-lock.yaml`) with no direct overlap files.
- Conflict resolution preserves both current-main ownership metadata (`senderIsOwner` stored under `__openclaw`) and this PR's trusted inbound-decoration contract (`inboundDecorated` / `bareBody`). The `before_message_write` redaction boundary still drops trusted inbound fields when hook output rewrites `content`, while preserving safe metadata such as `idempotencyKey` and `senderIsOwner`.
- Fresh validation from the synced head passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/pr95333-sync-core.tsbuildinfo`, the focused Vitest command covering transcript/UI/CLI/memory/LLM replay consumers, `git diff --check`, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/pr95333-sync-core-test.tsbuildinfo`, `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=8`, and the focused Mistral provider Vitest command all exited 0.
- The previously visible current-main baseline Mistral failure is fixed on the synced base; the focused `src/llm/providers/mistral.test.ts` run now passes locally (8/8 tests).

## 2026-06-28 rescue update

- Rebased the contributor branch onto current `origin/main` (`830467bc93`) and resolved the only manual conflict in `ui/src/ui/chat/message-extract.ts`, preserving both main's `isTextContentBlockType(...)` support and this PR's trusted bare-body extraction path.
- Fixed the current ClawSweeper P1 redaction-boundary blocker: `preparePersistedUserTurnMessageForTranscriptWrite(...)` now drops `inboundDecorated` / `bareBody` whenever a `before_message_write` hook rewrites user `content`, including spread-style redaction hooks. Added a regression test covering `{ ...message, content: "[redacted]" }`.
- Fixed the current ClawSweeper P1 type blocker: `resolveTrustedInboundBareBody(...)` now accepts any message-like object (`object | null | undefined`) and defensively reads the runtime-attached trusted fields, which removes the `TS2559` failures at the LLM-boundary and CLI imported-history call sites without requiring unsafe call-site casts. (An earlier attempt used a generic `<T extends object>`; that tripped `no-unnecessary-type-parameters` in `check-lint`, so the parameter is a plain `object`.)
- Kept memory-host session-file tests stable on Windows by asserting classification paths through the exported comparison normalizer and tolerating transient `EBUSY`/`ENOTEMPTY`/`EPERM` fixture cleanup during teardown. No cross-package import is added, so the memory-host-sdk private-package contract surface is unchanged (the `checks-fast-contracts-plugins-b` boundary check passes).
- Resolved the merge conflict: PR head is now `MERGEABLE` against `main`.

Additional verification after the rebase/repair:

```text
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
# exit=0

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo
# exit=0

node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts
# Test Files 1 passed; Tests 28 passed; exit=0

node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts
# Test Files 5 passed; Tests 145 passed; exit=0

node_modules/.bin/vitest run ui/src/ui/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts
# Test Files 3 passed; Tests 83 passed; exit=0

git diff --check
# exit=0
```

Local note: direct extension type-check targets were also attempted, but the local shared `node_modules` symlink is missing unrelated extension dependencies/exports (`@openclaw/crabline`, `acpx/runtime` members) in files outside this PR's diff; core production/test type-check targets for the touched code pass as shown above.

## Summary

- **What did NOT change:** This does not remove legacy sentinel stripping for already-persisted rows, does not migrate transcript files, does not change active-turn model prompt construction, and does not add unrelated provider/channel routing behavior.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users who paste or type literal metadata-looking text should not lose that text from the control UI, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory session corpus, or model historical replay when OpenClaw has a trusted bare body for the inbound turn.
- Behavior or issue addressed: user-authored text that looks like OpenClaw inbound metadata could be stripped or deduped incorrectly because consumers parsed forgeable sentinel text from `content`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/ui/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts`, `git diff --check`, a local `pnpm exec tsx` proof harness that persisted a real transcript row with `appendUserTurnTranscriptMessage(...)` then ran Control UI `normalizeMessage(...)` / `extractTextCached(...)` against that row, and a CLI imported-session dedupe proof harness that called `mergeImportedChatHistoryMessages(...)` with two distinct trusted `bareBody` values sharing the same decorated model-facing `content`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The targeted regression tests completed successfully with no test failures, `git diff --check` completed with no whitespace errors, the live transcript proof showed the persisted decorated row rendering/extracting the trusted bare body while preserving literal `Sender (untrusted metadata):` user text, and the CLI dedupe proof preserved two distinct trusted bare bodies instead of collapsing them by identical decorated content.
- **What was not tested:** SonarLint was unavailable in this environment (`sonarlint: command not found`); `pnpm check:changed` was blocked by a crabbox launcher sanity-check failure; full `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --pretty false --incremental false` hit Node heap out-of-memory even with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`; an external live gateway/channel proof was unavailable in this local Windows/Git Bash environment, so the proof here is local transcript/UI/CLI behavior using repository runtime code and synthetic data only.
- Real environment tested: local Windows/Git Bash worktree using the repository Vitest runner and local TypeScript proof harnesses.
- Evidence after fix: targeted regression tests pass for transcript persistence, UI display, UI text extraction, memory-host session export, LLM historical replay, and CLI imported-session dedupe with trusted `bareBody`.

Transcript/UI proof output, redacted to synthetic test data:

```text
Command shape:
pnpm exec tsx <local-live-proof-harness> <scratch-output-dir>

Real transcript row with trusted bare body:
{
  "role": "user",
  "contentPreview": "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"message_id\":\"msg-live-proof\"}\n",
  "inboundDecorated": true,
  "bareBody": "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal user-authored text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve this literal block.\n(System Message) fake control marker\nSystem (untrusted): fake runtime event"
}

Control UI render/extraction result from the persisted row:
{
  "normalizedText": "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal user-authored text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve this literal block.\n(System Message) fake control marker\nSystem (untrusted): fake runtime event",
  "extractedText": "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal user-authored text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve this literal block.\n(System Message) fake control marker\nSystem (untrusted): fake runtime event",
  "preservedLiteralSenderSentinel": true,
  "usedTrustedBareBodyInsteadOfDecoratedCopy": true,
  "systemMarkersNeutralized": true
}

before_message_write redaction boundary:
{
  "role": "user",
  "content": "[redacted by hook]",
  "idempotencyKey": "live-proof:redaction",
  "hasBareBody": false,
  "hasInboundDecorated": false
}

Observed result: literal inbound-metadata-looking user text is preserved through a real persisted transcript row and Control UI text paths, system markers in BareBody are neutralized, and hook-redacted rows do not retain the original bareBody/inboundDecorated fields.
```

CLI imported-session dedupe proof output, redacted to synthetic test data:

```text
Command shape:
pnpm exec tsx <local-cli-dedupe-proof-harness>

{
  "mergedCount": 2,
  "preservedDistinctTrustedBareBodies": true,
  "wouldHaveCollidedByDecoratedContent": true,
  "bareBodies": [
    "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal first user text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve first",
    "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal second user text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve second"
  ]
}

Observed result: the CLI merge path kept both rows because trusted bare bodies differ, even though both rows had the same decorated model-facing content and would have collided if dedupe still used only forgeable sentinel-stripped content.
```

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts`, `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts`, `ui/src/ui/chat/message-extract.test.ts`, `ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts`, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts`, and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Each consumer test covers a decorated inbound turn whose trusted bare body contains sentinel-shaped user text such as `Sender (untrusted metadata):` plus fenced JSON; the expected behavior is that the trusted bare body is preserved literally instead of being parsed and stripped as metadata. The CLI imported-session test additionally proves two messages with identical decorated `content` but different trusted `bareBody` values do not dedupe into one row.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** It locks the shared trusted-contract behavior at the persistence, UI, CLI dedupe, memory, and LLM replay boundaries without removing the legacy sentinel fallback or asserting unrelated prompt-construction details.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The parser/contract boundary was wrong: `buildInboundUserContextPrefix(...)` creates inbound metadata as plaintext blocks for model-facing prompts, and consumers such as UI history normalization, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session export, and LLM historical replay had no trusted way to distinguish host-added decoration from user-authored text in the same `content` channel.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The source-of-truth decision is no longer derived from forgeable `content` text. Consumers now use the shared trusted resolver and only accept `bareBody` when the message/context is explicitly marked `inboundDecorated: true` / `InboundDecorated: true`, so sentinel parsing remains only a legacy compatibility path.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix for a public/data-format contract bug.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High. The change is additive, keeps legacy fallback behavior, and has targeted regression coverage for the affected consumer paths.
- **Patch quality notes:** Dynamic `as unknown` casts stay at existing message-union boundaries where `AgentMessage` can carry additive metadata; guard/default returns preserve existing fallback behavior; the multi-file diff follows the shared consumer contract boundary and is not a downstream masking workaround.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The canonical contract is the inbound user-turn/message metadata (`inboundDecorated` plus `bareBody`, mirrored as `InboundDecorated` plus `BareBody` on inbound context). Display/history/CLI dedupe/memory consumers use that trusted contract when present and only parse text sentinels for unmarked legacy content.

## What Problem This Solves

Inbound context decoration is host-generated, but the decorated copy can live as text inside user-controlled user message content. Several consumers stripped or compared that decoration by matching forgeable sentinel strings such as `Sender (untrusted metadata):` and fenced JSON. If a user typed the same shape intentionally, downstream display/history/dedupe/memory paths could drop real user text or collapse distinct imported messages.

This PR gives consumers a trusted, out-of-band contract for decorated inbound turns: a message/context marker that says the content may be decorated, plus the host-authored bare body to render/replay/index/dedupe.

## Source-of-truth boundary

The canonical contract is the inbound user-turn/message metadata:

- runtime/persisted user messages: `inboundDecorated: true` plus `bareBody`
- inbound context: `InboundDecorated` plus `BareBody`

The model-facing prompt may still carry inbound context for the active turn. Display/history/CLI dedupe/memory consumers should use the trusted bare body when present, and only parse text sentinels for unmarked legacy content.

## Implementation summary

- Add optional trusted inbound fields:
  - `inboundDecorated: true` / `bareBody` on persisted/runtime user messages.
  - `InboundDecorated` / `BareBody` on inbound template context.
- Persist the trusted bare body on decorated user turns, while respecting `before_message_write` hooks as the redaction boundary: if a hook replaces content without returning trusted fields, the original `bareBody` / `inboundDecorated` is dropped.
- Update UI display, UI text extraction/export/search, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session indexing, and LLM historical replay to prefer the trusted bare body before falling back to legacy sentinel stripping.
- Keep existing `stripInboundMetadata(...)` behavior for old transcripts that do not carry the trusted fields.

## Scope boundary

In scope: contract/type plumbing for inbound user turns, transcript persistence/runtime merge preservation, UI display normalization, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session export/indexing, LLM historical replay normalization, and regression tests for those paths.

Out of scope: removing legacy sentinel stripping for already-persisted rows, changing active-turn model prompt construction, migrating existing transcript files, or doing a broad plugin SDK redesign beyond optional trusted fields.

## Related PR scan

The daily-fix related open PR scan found related PR #94419 as advisory background only. This PR does not depend on that work and keeps the fix scoped to the trusted inbound bare-body contract requested by #95279.

## Review findings addressed

- RF-001 / RF-004 / RF-007 / RF-008 — fixed in `src/gateway/cli-session-history.merge.ts`: the CLI imported-session comparable-text path now calls `resolveTrustedInboundBareBody(...)` for trusted decorated user messages before falling back to legacy sentinel stripping. Regression coverage: `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts` verifies two imported/local user turns with identical decorated content but distinct sentinel-shaped trusted bare bodies remain two messages.
- RF-002 / RF-003 — addressed with redacted terminal proof for the CLI imported-session dedupe path. The proof called `mergeImportedChatHistoryMessages(...)` with two trusted bare bodies and identical decorated content; output showed `mergedCount: 2`, `preservedDistinctTrustedBareBodies: true`, and `wouldHaveCollidedByDecoratedContent: true`.
- RF-005 / RF-006 — addressed by keeping the durable contract explicit and additive: `inboundDecorated` gates trust in `bareBody`, consumers use the shared resolver, legacy unmarked rows keep sentinel fallback behavior, and `before_message_write` remains the redaction boundary by dropping original trusted fields when hooks replace content without returning trusted fields themselves.
- RF-009 — passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts` completed successfully with no test failures.
- RF-010 — passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/ui/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/ui/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts` completed successfully with no test failures, and the same run was repeated including `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts` after the CLI dedupe fix was committed.
- RF-011 — passed: `git diff --check` completed with exit code 0 and no whitespace errors.
- Previous ClawSweeper P1 (`before_message_write` redaction boundary) — fixed in `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.ts`: `preparePersistedUserTurnMessageForTranscriptWrite(...)` now detects when a `before_message_write` hook rewrites the message `content` (the common `{ ...message, content: "[redacted]" }` spread pattern). When the hook's returned `content` differs from the incoming `content`, the persisted turn drops the original trusted `bareBody` and `inboundDecorated`, so downstream UI/replay/memory consumers can no longer trust text the hook meant to redact; idempotency keys are still preserved. Regression coverage: `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts` adds a case where a redaction hook returns `{ ...message, content: "[redacted by hook]" }` against a decorated secret prompt and asserts the persisted row has neither `bareBody` nor `inboundDecorated`.
- Previous ClawSweeper P1 (`BareBody` sanitizer) — fixed in `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-context.ts`: `BareBody` now uses the same inbound system-marker neutralization path as `RawBody` / `CommandBody` instead of newline-only trusted normalization. Regression coverage: `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts` asserts `[System Message]` and line-leading `System:` markers are neutralized on `BareBody`.
- Previous ClawSweeper UI extraction finding — fixed in `ui/src/ui/chat/message-extract.ts`: `extractText(...)` / `extractTextCached(...)` now use the shared `resolveTrustedInboundBareBody(...)` path for trusted decorated user messages before legacy sentinel stripping. Regression coverage: `ui/src/ui/chat/message-extract.test.ts` verifies sentinel-shaped user-authored text is preserved for export/search/text-extraction consumers.

## Verification

Passed locally (local Windows/Git Bash worktree, repository Vitest + tsgo runners):

- `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts` — 28 passed, including the new "drops trusted bare body when before_message_write spreads and rewrites content" case.
- `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts` — 60 passed.
- `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts` — 61 passed.

This file initially failed 3 `listSessionTranscriptCorpusEntriesForAgent` cases on Windows (`EBUSY` sqlite unlink + `C:\Windows\TEMP` vs `c:\windows\temp` path-case mismatch); the same 3 failed identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout. target.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.visibleReplies` is set to `message_tool`, the agent is expected to call the message tool to deliver replies. If the LLM forgets (a probabilistic event — the reporter saw it happen on the 8th turn after 7 correct deliveries), the reply was **silently discarded**: the substantive text sat in the JSONL transcript but was never delivered to the user.

The existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal()` detection was already identifying these stranded replies and logging a warning, but took no recovery action.

## Fix

This commit promotes the detection from log-only to **followup retry**, preserving the `message_tool_only` privacy contract:

1. **Gate room events**: Skip stranded reply detection for ambient `room_event` turns where `message_tool_only` is automatically set by the system. Silence on room events is intentional by design — the agent chose not to respond.

2. **Enqueue followup retry turn**: When a stranded reply is detected, enqueue a followup run whose prompt instructs the agent to deliver the captured text via `message(action=send)`. The agent itself calls the message tool, so delivery happens through the correct contract path — no suppression bypass, no privacy boundary crossing.

3. **Clear transcript/persistence fields**: The retry run explicitly clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` from the original followup run to prevent the original user prompt from hiding the retry instruction. The followup runner resolves `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text`, so a retained `transcriptPrompt` would cause the agent to see the original user question instead of the retry delivery instruction.

4. **No suppression bypass**: This does NOT mark payloads with `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or use `skipSuppressionCheck`. The `message_tool_only` privacy contract is fully preserved: delivery only happens when the agent explicitly calls `message(action=send)`.

Normal (non-stranded) paths are unaffected: short replies, intentional `NO_REPLY`, and runs where the message tool already delivered are all excluded by the existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal` guard.

### Why followup retry instead of bypass delivery?

The `message_tool_only` contract says: "no message tool call = private/silent". Auto-publishing stranded text would break this documented behavior. Instead, we give the agent a second chance to follow the contract correctly — like returning an undelivered letter and asking the sender to mail it properly, rather than opening and publishing it ourselves.

## Changed files

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — followup retry with cleaned transcript fields, room_event gate (+26/-3 net)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 5 new retry/gate tests replacing 6 bypass tests (-4 net)

## Tests

| Suite | Count | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` | 47 | ✅ All pass |
| `private-message-tool-final.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ All pass |
| `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | 189 | ✅ All pass (unchanged, confirms no regressions) |
| `followup-runner.test.ts` | 67 | ✅ All pass (confirms followup queue compatibility) |

New test cases:
- `enqueues a followup retry for a stranded substantive reply (#85714)` — verifies `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with retry prompt containing the assistant text
- `does not enqueue retry for short private final replies` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry when the message tool delivered this turn` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry for room_event turns (#85714)` — verifies room_event gate
- `clears transcriptPrompt on retry to prevent original prompt from hiding retry instruction (#85714)` — regression test verifying `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` are all `undefined` on the retry run

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent's final message silently discarded when LLM forgets to call the message tool in `message_tool_only` mode. The fix enqueues a followup retry turn so the agent can deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, patched checkout at `9dc3c76dc3`.
- **Privacy contract preserved**: The fix does NOT use `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or `skipSuppressionCheck`. No payload is auto-delivered. The agent is re-prompted to call `message(action=send)` itself.
- **Transcript isolation**: The retry run clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` so the followup runner's `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text` resolution correctly uses the retry prompt, not the original user message.
- **Room event safety**: Stranded reply detection is gated by `sessionCtx.InboundEventKind !== "room_event"`, so ambient room events (where silence is intentional) never trigger recovery. Covered by dedicated test case.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, `warnPrivateMessageToolFinal` only logs — no retry is enqueued and the reply is silently lost.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  ✓ auto-reply agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts (47 tests) 1729ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  47 passed (47)

  ✓ unit-fast private-message-tool-final.test.ts (8 tests) 2ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  8 passed (8)

  ✓ auto-reply dispatch-from-config.test.ts (189 tests) 3770ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  189 passed (189)

  ✓ auto-reply followup-runner.test.ts (67 tests) 1710ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  67 passed (67)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: When a stranded reply is detected, `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with a retry prompt containing the original assistant text and instructions to call `message(action=send)`. The retry run has `transcriptPrompt: undefined` so the followup runner correctly uses the retry instruction. Short replies, already-delivered replies, room events, and runs with existing transcript prompts are all verified by dedicated test cases.
- **What was not tested**: Live end-to-end delivery through an actual channel — the test verifies that the correct followup run is enqueued with the expected prompt shape and cleaned fields. The followup queue machinery (`enqueueFollowupRun` → `scheduleFollowupDrain` → `runReplyAgent`) is a well-tested existing mechanism used for concurrent message queuing.

## Real behavior proof (end-to-end, qa-lab host runner)

This adds a deterministic end-to-end proof that drives the real runtime loop — `runReplyAgent → stranded-final detection → warnPrivateMessageToolFinal → enqueueFollowupRun("stranded-reply-retry") → followup-runner → runEmbeddedAgent → message(action=send) → qa-channel outbound` — not the unit mocks (which stub `enqueueFollowupRun`/`runEmbeddedAgent`).

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Under `messages.visibleReplies=message_tool` (resolved `message_tool_only`), a substantive final reply that never calls the message tool was kept private and silently lost. The fix detects the stranded final and enqueues exactly one bounded followup retry that re-prompts the agent to deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract; if the retry strands again, no second retry is enqueued.
- **Real environment tested**: macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, branch `fix/stranded-reply-pending-delivery-85714` at current HEAD `0469009210` (rebased on latest upstream/main; recovery default-off + collect-batching isolation + updated scenario). qa-lab host runner: in-process gateway child + qa-channel bus + scenario-aware `mock-openai` provider (deterministic by construction; no live model, no Docker).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: ran the new scenario, PASS:
  ```
  node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite \
    --provider-mode mock-openai \
    --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-recovery \
    --concurrency 1 --fast
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: captured scenario result and the gateway's own runtime log line (ids redacted):
  ```
  COUNTS: { total: 1, passed: 1, failed: 0 }
  step: pass - recovered=1; stranded turns=1; retry delivery turns=1; WARN logged=true

  2026-06-06T06:31:23.411+08:00 [source-reply/private-final] agent produced a long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool (message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
  ```
  Asserted from the live request/outbound capture:
  - Turn 1 request: `plannedToolName !== "message"` (long plain-text final, stranded).
  - Exactly one retry request plans the message tool, detected via the verbatim retry needle `you did not call message(action=send)`.
  - Retry delivery request: `plannedToolName === "message"`, `plannedToolArgs.action === "send"`, `plannedToolArgs.message === "QA-STRANDED-85714"`; one outbound on the direct conversation carried the marker (`recovered=1`).
  - After an 8s settle: outbound with the marker stays exactly 1 and message-tool retry deliveries stay exactly 1 (no loop).
- **Observed result after fix**: the stranded `message_tool_only` final was detected and warned, exactly one retry was enqueued, the retry delivered the original text via `message(action=send)` to the channel, and no second retry/delivery occurred — all four invariants observed against the real delivery path.
- **What was not tested**: not run against a live frontier model (deterministic mock by design, since a real model "forgetting" the tool is non-deterministic), and not on a real chat transport (Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord) — exercised on the in-process qa-channel bus; the `message(action=send)` → source-conversation outbound contract is transport-agnostic core auto-reply behavior.

Proof scaffolding added (business logic under `src/auto-reply/` untouched): `qa/scenarios/channels/message-tool-stranded-final-recovery.md` (new scenario) and `extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.ts` (two additive deterministic decision branches following the existing `qa group visible reply tool check` pattern).

Closes #85714







## Update — retry drain scheduling (follow-up)

Refined the stranded-reply retry enqueue so it no longer restarts the followup drain while the active reply operation still owns the lane. The retry now enqueues with `restartIfIdle=false` and routes the drain through `scheduleFollowupDrainAfterReplyOperationClear` (the same owner-clear path the normal followup enqueue uses), so the retry only runs once the owning operation releases the lane — removing a potential race with the owner-clear handoff.

- **Changed**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — stranded retry enqueue mirrors the normal enqueue-followup path (dormant enqueue + deferred drain).
- **Test**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — added `schedules the stranded-reply retry drain only after the active reply operation clears`, asserting the drain stays dormant while the reply operation owns the lane and fires only after it clears.
- **Verification after this change** (local, macOS arm64, Node v24.10.0):
  ```
  vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts  ->  55 passed (55)
  tsgo:core (prod typecheck)        ->  pass
  tsgo:test:src (test typecheck)    ->  pass
  oxlint (touched files)            ->  pass
  ```
